# MongoDB sort and pagination optimization — vocabulary

> Terms of this concept, one per line: canonical name, relation to MongoDB sort and pagination optimization, definition where a source gives one, and the words people use instead (`aka:`). ## Terms

### blocking sort

- **blocking sort** · self — Check for a blocking sort with explain(): a SORT stage in the plan means a blocking sort; no SORT stage means the index supplies the order. Use hint() when testing candidate indexes. · aka: in-memory sort, in memory sort, SORT stage, sort stage, sort in memory, index-backed sort, sort with an index, sort uses an index, internalQueryMaxBlockingSortMemoryUsageBytes, 100 megabytes, 100 MB, sort exceeded memory limit, allowDiskUse, SORT_MERGE, sort merge, sort and limit, sort().limit, top-k sort — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/

### pagination

- **pagination** · part — Keyset pagination cannot jump to an arbitrary page, since reaching page N generally means visiting earlier pages, and it does not easily return total counts. It suits infinite scroll and next/previous navigation. Skip-limit suits shallow paging, small datasets and jump-to-page UIs. · aka: paginate, paging, skip(), cursor.skip, $skip, limit(), cursor.limit, $limit, skip and limit, offset pagination, keyset pagination, range pagination, cursor-based pagination, seek method, next page, page of results, deep skip — https://blog.openreplay.com/pagination-patterns-mongodb/

### query operator anti-pattern

- **query operator anti-pattern** · problem · aka: anti-pattern, anti-patterns, antipattern, unanchored regex, $regex, regular expression, case-insensitive regex, prefix expression, $ne, $nin, $not, negation, negated, inequality operator, $exists, $where, $expr, sargable, non-sargable

### $in

- **$in** · part — ESR guideline: $in used alone is an equality operator (a series of equality matches). With .sort(), an $in of fewer than 201 elements is expanded and merged in index sort order by a SORT_MERGE stage, behaving like equality; with 201 or more elements it is ordered like a range, subsequent index field · aka: $in operator, $or operator, $or clauses, clauses of $or, SUBPLAN, subplanner, index union, union of index scans, $or query, $or queries, $in list, $in array — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/

### projection

- **projection** · part · aka: project fields, projected fields, return only, exclude _id, _id: 0, $slice, $elemMatch projection, projection pushdown, covered query, covered queries, PROJECTION_COVERED, PROJECTION_SIMPLE, PROJECTION_DEFAULT

### count

- **count** · part — Keyset pagination cannot jump to an arbitrary page, since reaching page N generally means visiting earlier pages, and it does not easily return total counts. It suits infinite scroll and next/previous navigation. Skip-limit suits shallow paging, small datasets and jump-to-page UIs. · aka: countDocuments, estimatedDocumentCount, count(), db.collection.count, $count, COUNT_SCAN, count operations, db.collection.distinct, distinct(), DISTINCT_SCAN, $sample, random sample, pseudo-random cursor — https://blog.openreplay.com/pagination-patterns-mongodb/

### cursor

- **cursor** · part — cursor.allowDiskUse() has no effect on sort operations answered using an index or non-indexed ("in-memory") sort operations which require less than 100 megabytes of memory. For more complete documentation on in-memory sorts and sort index use, see Sort and Index Use. · aka: batchSize, batch size, cursor.batchSize, getMore, firstBatch, maxTimeMS, cursor.maxTimeMS, noCursorTimeout, cursor timeout, cursorTimeoutMillis, tailable cursor, maxAwaitTimeMS, exhaust cursor — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowDiskUse/

### read preference

- **read preference** · related · aka: readPreference, read preferences, secondary reads, secondaryPreferred, nearest, read concern, readConcern, local read concern, majority read concern, causal consistency

### sharded query targeting

- **sharded query targeting** · part · aka: targeted query, targeted queries, targeted operations, scatter-gather, scatter gather, broadcast operations, broadcast query, query router, mongos, SHARD_MERGE, SHARDING_FILTER, shard targeting, single shard, all shards, merge on mongos, $lookup on sharded, include the shard key, shard key in the query, query isolation

### query shape

- **query shape** · related · aka: query shapes, query pattern, query patterns, query predicate, query selector

### index

- **index** · related — To use an index for string sorting, the operation must specify the same collation as the index; a different collation means the index cannot supply the string order and a blocking sort results. · aka: indexes, indexed, IXSCAN, COLLSCAN, collection scan, explain, executionStats, winningPlan — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes/

### query optimization

- **query optimization** · hypernym · aka: query performance, optimize queries, query optimizer, analyze query performance
